reading.title: Farms on the roof
reading.text: Singapore imports more than 90 percent of its food, so the government has started to offer grants to rooftop farms. The idea is not to replace imports but to transfer some production closer to consumers. Supporters refer to studies showing that city farms can grow vegetables using far less water than fields, even without fertile soil. Opinions differ, however, on how much these farms can really produce. From early figures, analysts infer that rooftop farms supply less than five percent of the vegetables the city needs, but they also create jobs and teach young people where food comes from.

items.q: Why does the Singapore government support rooftop farms?
o: To move some production closer to consumers

items.q: What do supporters say about city farms?
o: They use much less water than fields.
Rooftop farms meet most of the city's needs.
Rooftop farms supply only a small share of vegetables.
